title: Directed Clinical Practice IV
description: This course is the fourth clinical experience in the Neurodiagnostic Technology Program and takes place at an affiliated healthcare facility. The emphasis for this course is on evoked potential (EP), advanced skills in electroencephalographic (EEG) recording and analysis, and more specialized diagnostic testing procedures (as available). The specialized areas may include intraoperative neurophysiologic monitoring (IONM), neonatal testing, long-term epilepsy monitoring, pediatric tests, transcranial doppler (TCD) studies, nerve conduction (NCV) studies and others. The clinical experience provides students a supervised application of previously learned techniques and skills at an advanced level and progressing toward entry level. The focus is on safe, legal and professional behavior. This course also fosters the development of communication skills and interpersonal relationships required for the healthcare field. Supervision of the students is provided by a neurodiagnostic technologist and/or physician of the affiliating institution and is coordinated by the college faculty. This course is designed for students enrolled in the Neurodiagnostic Technology Program.
outcomes: Students will continue to gain valuable clinical experience by measuring and applying EEG electrodes, and monitoring patients in advance clinical settings such as ICU and LTM units.

Their skills will be evaluated by improvements in the recognition of mechanical and physiological artifacts, normal wake and sleep patterns, abnormal focal and generalized patterns, and EEG interpretation formulation up to 85-95 % accuracy.
objectives: Demonstrate professional behavior including willingness to adhere to policies, appropriate dress code, and absence/tardiness reporting guidelines.
Conduct self in an appropriate ethical manner as a health care professional including maintaining patient confidentiality and safety at all times.
Seek instruction and use feedback to improve performance.
Relate to patients in a positive manner to encourage patient cooperation and enhance attitude including good communication skills in explaining all procedures and expectations of the patient.
Maintain work area in an orderly manner. Obtain and replace supplies as needed and keep work areas neat and clean.

Calibrate the machine with 100% accuracy and ability to make all necessary adjustments to the instrument for accurate recordings, including the proper use of cal voltage related to sensitivities and calibrating all settings used during a test.
Take valid patient data.
Identify artifacts with 100% accuracy.
Identify normal rhythms, including sleep, with 100% accuracy.
Use machine settings (including filters, sensitivity, etc.) accurately and when necessary.
Apply electrodes accurately within 20-25 minutes, and get the patients test performed in an acceptable time as per the lab schedule.
Monitor artifacts with 100% accuracy.
Identify abnormalities with 90% accuracy.
Justify appropriate use of montages with 90% accuracy.
Write a description of each EEG at an acceptable level when reviewed by the technologist.
Explain each test procedure clearly, and obtain optimal patient cooperation.
Apply electrodes accurately with respect to each modality tested.
Recall basic components of lab protocols in each of the modalities.
Take valid patient histories.
Identify and measure important data from EP waveforms.
Make necessary calculations for physician interpretations.
Set up EP equipment to the desired protocols for each modality.
Recognize and remedy artifacts on the EP.
Utilize the appropriate stimulus for each modality.
Recall basics of the lab's normative data for comparison and evaluation of normal versus abnormal.

Observe and perform as much of the various testing as possible. Students should obtain exposure to as many of the following as possible: quantitative EEG & EP (mapping), telemetry, ambulatory EEG, polysomnography, surgical monitoring application of EEG & EP, NCV, ENG, TCD, etc.
